text: There is breaking news out of the Middle East and Iran has fired ballistic missiles in the
direction of US troops. This just coming through in the last couple of moments. Let's go live to
the White House. Our man on the ground there, Jonathan Kersley. What is the Pentagon saying
about this, Jono? Fascinating, Laura, that after days of no strikes from either Iran or the United
States on each other, we are hearing this from US Central Command. In a statement issued just
a short time ago, they say the following at 5.45pm Eastern Time today. So this was around
about an hour and 15 minutes ago these attacks happened. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps
forces launched multiple ballistic missiles from Iran in an attempted surprise attack on
US forces based in the Middle East. All Iranian missiles were successfully intercepted. US
forces remained vigilant and at a high state of readiness. It has been reported that these
missiles were fired in the direction of Jordan and a US base in that country. We know there
had been Iranian strikes in that region previously. In Jordan, that was where three US service personnel
lost their lives almost two weeks ago in an attack on a base there and it increased the
American casualties. The real question now, Laura, in the wake of this latest move by the IRGC is
how is that going to destabilise the talks that have been going on behind the scenes? The United States
have been saying that they would respond kind for kind. Well, let's see now in the hours ahead how
Donald Trump and his administration is going to respond to this from the Iran Revolutionary Guard
Corps. President Trump, Laura, today had been hosting leaders of nations from two wars,
Vladimir Zelensky from Ukraine, where they talked about Patriot missiles to defend Russia,
and then Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. And of course, the conflict with Iran very much
front of mind in that conversation that lasted round about 90 minutes in the Oval Office. Both
leaders arriving via the West Wing private entrance, no television cameras inside. Unusual and perhaps
a sign too of the kinds of discussions they wanted to have behind closed doors on this occasion.
There has been much talk between the United States and Israel about how to prevent Iran getting a
nuclear weapon. Now, Prime Minister Netanyahu said after this meeting today, as far as he's concerned,
this was his best one yet with President Trump. This is some of a video message he put out after
these talks today. I just finished an excellent meeting with President Trump. When I say excellent,
it's not just lip service. A conversation with full partnership, mutual support, understanding of the
common goal to ensure that Iran does not have nuclear weapons and other goals as well. This is one of the best
conversations I have had with the President of the US, our friend, President Donald Trump.
But once again tonight, as night falls here in the United States, Laura, there could be more concerns
about where the conflict with Iran could be going to next. Just repeating that news, the Iran Revolutionary Guard
Corps has fired four ballistic missiles in what US Central Command is saying is an attempted surprise attack
on a US base in Jordan. Those four missiles all intercepted by the United States, Laura.
